test_cases.title: Baro App Executes at 20 Hz Cadence
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with mock baro library and software bus. Configure a fake monotonic time source advancing at 1 microsecond resolution.
procedure: Drive the TDM scheduler tick for a simulated duration of 1.000 seconds.
Capture the timestamp of every baro app Execute() invocation.
Compute the inter-execution period from consecutive timestamps.
Compute the total number of executions during the 1 second window.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Baro app Execute() is invoked exactly 20 times in 1 simulated second with inter-execution period of 50 ms +/- 1 ms.

test_cases.title: One Baro Sample Acquired Per Cycle
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with a stubbed baro_lib returning programmed pressure/temperature/altitude values and counting sample-acquisition calls, and a recording bus broker to capture published baro messages.
procedure: Reset the mock baro library acquisition counter to zero.
Invoke baro app Execute() exactly N=10 times.
Read the mock baro library acquisition counter.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Mock baro library reports exactly 10 sample-acquisition calls after 10 Execute() invocations (one sample per cycle, no missed or duplicated reads).

test_cases.title: Baro Message Published Each Cycle
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with a stubbed baro_lib returning programmed pressure/temperature/altitude values, and a recording bus broker that captures all publish() calls and their topic identifiers.
procedure: Subscribe a test observer to the baro message topic on the mock bus.
Invoke baro app Execute() exactly N=5 times.
Inspect the observer's received message queue.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Test observer receives exactly 5 baro messages on the baro topic, one per Execute() invocation.

test_cases.title: Pass-Through Pressure Without Filtering
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with a stubbed baro_lib configured to return a scripted sequence of distinct pressure/temperature/altitude values, and a recording bus broker to capture published baro messages.
procedure: Configure mock baro library to return pressure values [101325.0, 101300.0, 101275.0, 101250.0, 101225.0] Pa over 5 cycles.
Invoke baro app Execute() 5 times.
Capture the pressure field from each published baro message in order.
Compare each published pressure value to the corresponding mock input value bit-for-bit.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each published baro message pressure field equals the corresponding mock library input exactly (bitwise identical, no filtering or smoothing applied).

test_cases.title: Pass-Through Altitude Without Filtering
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with a stubbed baro_lib configured to return a scripted sequence of distinct pressure/temperature/altitude values, and a recording bus broker to capture published baro messages.
procedure: Configure mock baro library to return altitude values [100.0, 110.0, 120.0, 130.0, 140.0] m over 5 cycles.
Invoke baro app Execute() 5 times.
Capture the altitude field from each published baro message.
Compare each published altitude value to the corresponding mock input value bit-for-bit.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each published baro message altitude field equals the corresponding mock library input exactly (no filtering or modification).

test_cases.title: Monotonic Microsecond Timestamp Present
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with a fake monotonic time source advancing in microsecond resolution, a stubbed baro_lib returning programmed pressure/temperature/altitude values, and a recording bus broker to capture published baro messages.
procedure: Invoke baro app Execute() 10 times with simulated 50 ms gaps between calls.
Capture the timestamp field from each published baro message.
Verify each timestamp is strictly greater than the previous timestamp.
Verify timestamp units are microseconds by comparing the delta between consecutive timestamps to the simulated 50 ms interval.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All 10 published baro message timestamps are strictly monotonically increasing, and consecutive deltas equal 50000 microseconds +/- 1000.

test_cases.title: Baro Health Published Each Cycle
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with mock baro library reporting a configurable health status, and a mock software bus that records publish() calls per topic.
procedure: Subscribe a test observer to the baro health topic on the mock bus.
Configure mock baro library to alternate health between NOMINAL and DEGRADED across cycles.
Invoke baro app Execute() exactly N=6 times.
Inspect the observer's received baro health message queue.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Test observer receives exactly 6 baro health messages whose status field matches the mock library health value for each corresponding cycle.

test_cases.title: Baro Message Schema References WGS-84 HAE
test_cases.setup: Open the baro message header (struct or schema definition) used by baro_app and any associated documentation comments.
procedure: Locate the altitude field declaration in the baro message struct.
Inspect the field comment, units annotation, and reference frame documentation.
Verify the comment states 'WGS-84 ellipsoid' or 'HAE' (height above ellipsoid).
Verify there is no conflicting reference (e.g., MSL, AGL) in the same field's documentation.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Baro message altitude field is documented as WGS-84 ellipsoid (HAE) with no conflicting reference frame, confirmed by reviewer inspection.

expected_artifacts.name: baro_app_hae_inspection.md
expected_artifacts.description: Signed inspection record verifying HAE altitude reference convention

test_cases.title: Baro Message Units Are Pascals and Meters
test_cases.setup: Open the baro message struct/schema definition and any unit-related documentation.
procedure: Locate the pressure field declaration in the baro message struct.
Verify pressure field is documented in pascals (Pa).
Locate the altitude field declaration in the baro message struct.
Verify altitude field is documented in meters (m).
Verify no scaling factor or alternate unit is applied in baro_app source between baro lib output and bus publish.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Baro message pressure field is documented in pascals and altitude field in meters, with no scaling applied in baro_app prior to publication.

expected_artifacts.name: baro_app_si_units_inspection.md
expected_artifacts.description: Signed inspection record verifying SI units (Pa, m) in baro message

test_cases.title: POSIX vs Pico2 Build Functional Equivalence
test_cases.setup: Build baro_app for POSIX target and use the recorded Pico2 reference output. Prepare a fixed deterministic input sample stream, with a stubbed baro_lib returning programmed pressure/temperature/altitude values, and a recording bus broker to capture published baro messages.
procedure: Feed the identical fixed input sample stream (N=200 samples) to the POSIX baro_app build via mock baro library.
Capture all published baro messages from the POSIX run, excluding wall-clock-derived timestamp fields.
Compare each captured field (pressure, altitude, health, sample index) against the recorded Pico2 reference output for the same input stream.
Compute byte-for-byte equality on the message field set excluding timestamps.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All 200 POSIX-published baro messages match the Pico2 reference output exactly across pressure, altitude, and health fields.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Output for Identical Inputs
test_cases.setup: Instantiate two independent baro app instances with identical configuration, each with a stubbed baro_lib returning programmed pressure/temperature/altitude values from the same scripted sample sequence, and a recording bus broker to capture published baro messages.
procedure: Feed the identical scripted sample sequence (N=100 samples) into both baro app instances.
Invoke Execute() 100 times on each instance under an identical fake clock schedule.
Capture all published baro messages from both instances.
Compare the two message streams byte-for-byte across all fields including timestamps.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Both instances produce 100 published baro messages that are byte-for-byte identical across every field.

test_cases.title: Re-Run Determinism Across Repeated Executions
test_cases.setup: Instantiate a baro app with a stubbed baro_lib returning programmed pressure/temperature/altitude values from a fixed scripted sample sequence, a fake monotonic clock, and a recording bus broker to capture published baro messages.
procedure: Invoke Execute() 100 times and capture all published baro messages as run A.
Tear down and re-instantiate the baro app with identical configuration and identical scripted inputs.
Invoke Execute() 100 times and capture all published baro messages as run B.
Compare run A and run B byte-for-byte.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Run A and run B produce byte-for-byte identical sequences of 100 baro messages.

test_cases.title: Sample-To-Publish Ordering Preserved Per Cycle
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with mock baro library and mock software bus, both recording call order with timestamps.
procedure: Invoke baro app Execute() once.
Inspect the recorded call sequence on the mock baro library and the mock bus.
Verify the baro library sample acquisition was called before the bus publish call within the same Execute() cycle.
Repeat the check for 5 cycles.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: In every Execute() cycle the sample-acquire call precedes the publish call, and exactly one of each occurs per cycle.

test_cases.title: Health Bitmap Reflects Library Fault Injection
test_cases.setup: Instantiate baro app with mock baro library exposing an injectable fault bitmap and a mock software bus.
procedure: Inject fault bitmap value 0x00 (no faults) into the mock baro library; invoke Execute() once; capture published health.
Inject fault bitmap value 0x01 (sensor fault) into the mock baro library; invoke Execute() once; capture published health.
Inject fault bitmap value 0xFF into the mock baro library; invoke Execute() once; capture published health.
Compare each published health bitmap to the injected value.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each published baro health message bitmap field equals the corresponding injected fault bitmap exactly (0x00, 0x01, 0xFF).
